recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if MnM later decides the actual code must be the literal mnemonic IMMEDIATE instead of the existing FHIR code IMD with display Immediate.
issue_request: FHIR-19344 asked how to represent an immediate dose when MedicationRequest has one request-level priority but multiple dosageInstructions. The final Published/Persuasive resolution was to add an Immediate timing code to http://hl7.org/fhir/event-timing for use through Timing.repeat.when, rather than moving MedicationRequest.priority.
initial_application: The change was applied in c4807a5165ee632872ef9f6289fee8e9e1abbb5f, a March 2021 R5 MnM batch commit that explicitly listed FHIR-19344 and added the IMD/Immediate row with the requested definition to source/datatypes/timing.xml. A same-day follow-up, 6314862f6c410bf17b0136e5e54e1d20b7c2d5c3, removed a transient timing-abbreviation CodeSystem file while keeping codes directly in the Timing spreadsheet.
additional_context: The active current source has Timing.repeat.when bound to EventTiming and defines EventTiming from #event-timing in source/datatypes/timing.xml. The R5 and current CI CodeSystem event-timing JSON both include IMD with display Immediate and the requested definition. Searches of Zulip and Confluence found no evidence changing the Jira/source interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current authoritative Timing source, R5 publication surface, and current build surface already carry the resolved EventTiming code; retaining MedicationRequest.priority is consistent with the Jira resolution.
